record.what_it_does: Hosted REST API and MCP server for YouTube transcripts, search, channel and playlist data.
record.auth_notes: REST uses a Bearer API key from the dashboard. The MCP server supports OAuth (Claude, ChatGPT). Each end user would need their own TranscriptAPI account and key, or the toolkit would use a single shared key.
record.access_notes: Signup gives 100 free credits with no card. Paid plans are $5/month for 1,000 credits or $54/year. Top-ups are available. Rate limit is 200 requests/min on the monthly plan.
record.api_breadth_notes: 13 read-only GET endpoints: transcript, video info/metadata, search, channel (resolve, info, search, videos, playlists, posts, sections, latest), and playlist videos.
record.blocker_notes: The API is small and read-only, and it is a paid-per-credit service. No OpenAPI file was found, but the docs link a Swagger UI at /swagger.

evidence.quote: New accounts get 100 free credits with no card required

record.needs_human: The OpenAPI spec was not confirmed. A Swagger UI exists at /swagger, so a JSON spec probably exists behind it. The MCP URL and the 100-free-credits claim come from the landing page as summarized by the fetch tool. I did not open the MCP docs page. The hint (transcriptapi.com) was followed.
